notes: EBIT proxy: using 'Operating income' from the consolidated income statement (assumed to represent EBIT for the pipeline). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000000296925000055/apd-20250930.htm))
D&A proxy: using 'Depreciation and amortization' from the consolidated cash flow statement. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000000296925000055/apd-20250930.htm))

Capex proxy: using the company-defined 'Capital Expenditures' non-GAAP measure (includes certain investments and excludes NEOM Green Hydrogen Company expenditures not funded by Air Products’ equity), which can make capex% sales appear unusually high versus simpler capex definitions. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000000296925000055/apd-20250930.htm))

NWC definition: modeled as (Total Current Assets - Total Current Liabilities) from the consolidated balance sheet (does not exclude cash or investments beyond what is captured in current assets/curr liabilities). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000000296925000055/apd-20250930.htm))

Tax rate: base-case tax_rate uses an adjusted effective tax-rate level implied by the FY2025/FY2024 effective tax context; set as 0.18. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000000296925000055/apd-20250930.htm))

NOL utilization: NOL utilization percent is not explicitly disclosed; set to null (nol_balance includes U.S. state and foreign net operating loss carryforwards totaling $578.3M as of 30 September 2025). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000000296925000055/apd-20250930.htm))

Terminal exit multiple selection: based on peer EV/EBITDA level ranges from MarketScreener comp tables, with a modest premium for Air Products quality/scale; terminal_exit_ebitda_multiple set to 14.0. ([marketscreener.com](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/LINDE-PLC-46923083/valuation/))
Current price: uses the latest available finance snapshot (APD = $281.01; latest trade time shown as March 20 UTC).

catalysts: Project execution updates (cost, commissioning pace) that change the expected capex trajectory and long-run operating profile.
Improving helium pricing and/or broader industrial demand signals that can lift revenue and operating leverage.
Potential changes to capital allocation priorities as management refines the clean energy transition roadmap.
company_overview: Global industrial gases producer with a contract-based model spanning energy, environmental, and emerging markets.
Operational footprint and scale support margin durability and capacity-led growth in multiple regions.
Clean energy investments (e.g., hydrogen-related initiatives) are a key driver of multi-year capital allocation.
current_context: In fiscal Q1 2026, Air Products reported first-quarter sales of $3.1B (+6% y/y) and GAAP operating income of $735M (+14% y/y). ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/air-products-reports-fiscal-2026-first-quarter-results-302674978.html?utm_source=openai))

Company commentary emphasized mix/pricing support and cost actions as the primary drivers of the quarter’s operating performance. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/air-products-reports-fiscal-2026-first-quarter-results-302674978.html?utm_source=openai))

The stock setup reflects ongoing execution risk tied to project optimization while the core industrial gases base seeks to maintain earnings conversion. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/air-products-reports-fiscal-2026-first-quarter-results-302674978.html?utm_source=openai))
investment_highlights: Base-case thesis assumes modest revenue growth consistent with historical low-to-mid single digit trends and contract pricing/mix.
EBIT margin is projected to remain near normalized levels (target ~0.38), supported by productivity and pricing discipline.

Capital intensity is elevated in the near term due to the clean energy project cycle, with capex%-of-sales stepping down over the forecast horizon as the ramp matures. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2969/000000296925000055/apd-20250930.htm))
Working capital is modeled using a conservative net working capital ratio (NWC as current assets minus current liabilities), stabilizing near ~0.29–0.30 of sales.
key_risks: Clean energy and project execution risk (cost overruns, delays, exit actions) impacting margin and cash generation.
Working-capital volatility (receivables/payables timing) that can pressure near-term free cash flow conversion.
Macro/FX/feedstock volatility and discount-rate changes that can compress valuation multiples.
